test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-II Official Paper (Held On: 20 Dec, 2025)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three approaches of the Government of India for poverty reduction?

options.text: Growth-oriented approach with the expectation that economic growth would trickle down to the poor.
Raise incomes and employment for the poor by creating additional assets and by means of work generation.
Ensure the bare minimum level of remuneration or wage for labour with different levels of skills.
Provide minimum basic amenities to people through public expenditure on social consumption needs.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Ensure the bare minimum level of remuneration or wage for labour with different levels of skills.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Government of India has adopted **three primary approaches** for poverty reduction:
 
• **Growth-oriented approach:** Focuses on economic growth with the belief that the benefits of growth will trickle down to the poor. *Hence, this approach is correct.*
 
• **Asset creation and employment generation:** Aims to raise incomes and employment for the poor by creating additional assets and generating work opportunities. *Hence, this approach is correct.*
 
• **Provision of basic amenities:** Ensures access to minimum basic amenities such as healthcare, education, and housing through public expenditure on social consumption needs. *Hence, this approach is correct.*
 
• The **statement about ensuring the bare minimum remuneration** for labour is not a comprehensive poverty reduction strategy but rather a labour policy initiative under minimum wage laws. Therefore, it **does not qualify** as one of the three approaches. *Hence, this is the correct answer.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Growth-Oriented Approach:**

 
 
• This approach emphasizes economic growth as a means to reduce poverty.
 
• The idea is to generate wealth and increase income levels, which will eventually benefit the poor.
 
• For example, liberalization policies initiated in **1991** focused on economic growth, indirectly reducing poverty.
 
 
 
• **Asset Creation and Employment Generation:**
 
 
• Programs like the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), 2005**, aim to provide rural employment and create durable assets.
 
• Such schemes are targeted at improving the livelihood of the poorest sections of society by generating work opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Provision of Basic Amenities:**
 
 
• Programs such as **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY)**, **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan**, and **National Health Mission (NHM)** ensure access to housing, sanitation, and healthcare for the poor.
 
• These initiatives aim to improve the living standards of people below the poverty line by addressing their basic needs.
 
 
 
• **Minimum Wage Laws:**
 
 
• The statement about ensuring a bare minimum remuneration for labour is a reference to labour laws like the **Minimum Wages Act, 1948**.
 
• This act ensures that workers are paid at least the minimum wage for their work based on skill levels, preventing exploitation.
 
• While important, it is not classified as a poverty reduction strategy but as a measure for ensuring fair labour practices.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **MGNREGA:** Provides at least **100 days of guaranteed wage employment** in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.
 
• **National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP):** Aims to provide support to aged, widowed, disabled, and families in extreme poverty through financial assistance.
 
• **Public Distribution System (PDS):** Ensures food security by distributing essential commodities like rice, wheat, and kerosene at subsidized prices.
 
• **Minimum Wages Act, 1948:** Protects workers from being underpaid by fixing minimum wages for different categories of work.
